setup_instructions.step_1: Create empty folder for new workspace: mkdir healthtrack-mongodb && cd healthtrack-mongodb
setup_instructions.step_3: Checkout target branch: git checkout mongodb-electron-optimized
setup_instructions.step_4: Create new development branch: git checkout -b mongodb-development
setup_instructions.step_6: Copy environment variables from .env.example or ask for them
setup_instructions.step_7: Start web app: npm run dev OR Start Electron app: npm run electron:dev
setup_instructions.step_8: Verify setup by visiting http://localhost:3000 or launching Electron window

what_to_ask_handoff_person: Any specific team conventions or coding standards
Preferred branch naming or commit message format
Access to MongoDB Atlas cluster (if needed)
Google Cloud/Vertex AI credentials and project setup
NOTE: Git repository URL is now included above - no need to ask
first_verification_steps: After setup, run 'npm run dev' - should see Next.js start on port 3000
Visit http://localhost:3000 - should see HealthTrack-AI landing page
Try 'npm run electron:dev' - should launch Electron window
Check console for any MongoDB connection errors
Navigate to /dashboard - should show empty patient list
Try creating a new patient case to verify database works

development_guidelines.database_access: Always use src/lib/mongodb functions - never direct MongoDB client
development_guidelines.collection_routing: Framework automatically routes to local/remote - no manual selection needed
development_guidelines.electron_db: Local MongoDB runs on port 27018 via mongodb-memory-server
development_guidelines.patient_data: Stored locally for privacy - only MIMIC-IV data is remote
development_guidelines.vector_search: Uses MongoDB Atlas vector search for case similarity
development_guidelines.testing: Use test files in root directory for IPC and SOAP functionality

critical_files_to_understand.electron/db/sqlite-db.ts: DO NOT USE - This is SQLite from parallel track
critical_files_to_understand.electron/ipc/database-handlers.ts: IPC handlers for Electron database operations

what_to_avoid.sqlite_files: Ignore all SQLite-related files - they're from the parallel development track
what_to_avoid.framework_modification: Don't modify the dual-database framework without understanding full impact
what_to_avoid.direct_mongodb: Never use MongoDB client directly - always use the abstraction layer
what_to_avoid.remote_patient_data: Never store patient data in remote database for privacy

immediate: Verify all MongoDB operations work correctly
Test Electron app with local database
short_term: Enhance SOAP notes parsing and validation

testing_strategy.ipc_testing: Use test-ipc-handlers-clean.js for Electron IPC verification
testing_strategy.database_testing: test-sqlite-db.js contains general DB testing patterns
testing_strategy.manual_testing: Start with /dashboard page and create a new patient case

troubleshooting_common_issues.mongodb_connection: Check MONGODB_URI and network connectivity to Atlas
troubleshooting_common_issues.electron_db: Ensure mongodb-memory-server starts correctly on port 27018
troubleshooting_common_issues.vertex_ai: Verify all GCP environment variables are set correctly
troubleshooting_common_issues.ipc_errors: Check electron/ipc/database-handlers.ts for proper error handling

Performance issues with large patient datasets

Integration with new AI models or APIs
